sections.body:
```python
print("\nExample 2: Perfectly Dependent Variables")
X_dep = np.random.randint(0, 4, n_samples)
Y_dep = X_dep.copy()  # Y = X

mi_perfect = calculate_mi_discrete(X_dep, Y_dep)
h_x = -np.sum([np.sum(X_dep == i)/n_samples * np.log2(np.sum(X_dep == i)/n_samples) 
               for i in range(4)])

print(f"  Y = X (perfect dependence)")
print(f"  MI(X;Y) = {mi_perfect:.4f} bits")
print(f"  H(X) = {h_x:.4f} bits")
print(f"  MI = H(X)? {abs(mi_perfect - h_x) < 0.01} ✓")
```

sections.title: Example 4: Feature selection (real Ml use case)
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- COMPLETE EXAMPLE 1: Decision Tree Splits using Information Gain…
- Calculate entropy of labels
- Calculate information gain for a split
- COMPLETE EXAMPLE 2: Feature Selection using Mutual Information…
- Calculate MI between each feature and target
- Plot 1: Venn diagram showing MI
- Circles for H(X) and H(Y)
- Plot 2: MI for different dependence levels

**Defines:** `calculate_entropy()`, `information_gain()`, `softmax()`, `cross_entropy_loss()`

```python
print("\nExample 4: Feature Selection with MI")
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif

iris = load_iris()
X_iris = iris.data
y_iris = iris.target

# Calculate MI between each feature and target
mi_scores = mutual_info_classif(X_iris, y_iris, random_state=42)

print(f"  Iris dataset - MI with target:")
for i, (name, score) in enumerate(zip(iris.feature_names, mi_scores)):
    print(f"    {name}: MI = {score:.4f}")

print(f"\n  Best feature: {iris.feature_names[np.argmax(mi_scores)]}")

# Visualizations
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10))

# Plot 1: Venn diagram showing MI
from matplotlib.patches import Circle
axes[0, 0].set_xlim(0, 10)
axes[0, 0].set_ylim(0, 10)
axes[0, 0].set_aspect('equal')

# Circles for H(X) and H(Y)
circle_X = Circle((3.5, 5), 2, color='blue', alpha=0.3, label='H(X)')
circle_Y = Circle((6.5, 5), 2, color='red', alpha=0.3, label='H(Y)')
axes[0, 0].add_patch(circle_X)
axes[0, 0].add_patch(circle_Y)

# Labels
axes[0, 0].text(2.5, 5, 'H(X|Y)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', ha='center')
axes[0, 0].text(7.5, 5, 'H(Y|X)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', ha='center')
axes[0, 0].text(5, 5, 'I(X;Y)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', ha='center',
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='yellow'))

# Equations
axes[0, 0].text(5, 8.5, 'I(X;Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X,Y)', fontsize=11, ha='center',
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='lightblue'))
axes[0, 0].text(5, 1.5, 'I(X;Y) = H(X) - H(X|Y) = H(Y) - H(Y|X)', fontsize=11, ha='center',
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='lightgreen'))

axes[0, 0].set_title('Mutual Information: Shared Information', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].axis('off')

# Plot 2: MI for different dependence levels
dependence_levels = ['Independent', '20% Noise', '10% Noise', 'Perfect\nDep']

colors_dep = ['red', 'orange', 'yellow', 'green']

bars = axes[0, 1].bar(dependence_levels, mi_values, color=colors_dep, 
                       alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black', linewidth=2)

axes[0, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

for bar, mi in zip(bars, mi_values):
    height = bar.get_height()
    axes[0, 1].text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, height + 0.05, 
                    f'{mi:.3f}', ha='center', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')

# Plot 3: Feature importance (Iris)
feature_importance = axes[1, 0].barh(iris.feature_names, mi_scores, 
                                      color='steelblue', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Mutual Information with Target', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_title('Feature Selection: Iris Dataset', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='x')

for i, (name, score) in enumerate(zip(iris.feature_names, mi_scores)):
    axes[1, 0].text(score + 0.02, i, f'{score:.3f}', va='center', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')

# Plot 4: MI vs Correlation
# Generate data with different relationships
np.random.seed(42)
x = np.random.randn(300)

# Linear relationship
y_linear = 2*x + np.random.randn(300)*0.5

# Non-linear relationship

# Calculate correlations and MI
from scipy.stats import pearsonr
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_regression

corr_linear = abs(pearsonr(x, y_linear)[0])

methods = ['Linear\nRelationship', 'Non-linear\nRelationship']

               width_methods, label='Pearson Correlation', 
               color='lightcoral', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')

               width_methods, label='Mutual Information', 
               color='lightblue', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')

"""
================================================================================
COMPLETE EXAMPLE 1: Decision Tree Splits using Information Gain
================================================================================
"""

print("\n" + "="*80)
print("COMPLETE EXAMPLE 1: Decision Tree - Information Gain")
print("="*80)

def calculate_entropy(labels):
    """Calculate entropy of labels"""
    _, counts = np.unique(labels, return_counts=True)
    probs = counts / len(labels)
    return -np.sum(probs * np.log2(probs + 1e-10))

def information_gain(data, labels, feature_idx, threshold):
    """Calculate information gain for a split"""
    # Parent entropy
    parent_entropy = calculate_entropy(labels)
    
    # Split data
    left_mask = data[:, feature_idx] <= threshold
    right_mask = ~left_mask
    
    if np.sum(left_mask) == 0 or np.sum(right_mask) == 0:
        return 0.0
    
    # Children entropies
    left_entropy = calculate_entropy(labels[left_mask])
    right_entropy = calculate_entropy(labels[right_mask])
    
    # Weighted average
    n = len(labels)
    n_left = np.sum(left_mask)
    n_right = np.sum(right_mask)
    
    child_entropy = (n_left/n) * left_entropy + (n_right/n) * right_entropy
    
    # Information gain
    return parent_entropy - child_entropy

# Example dataset
X_tree = np.array([
    [1, 1], [1, 2], [2, 1], [2, 2],  # Class 0
    [4, 4], [4, 5], [5, 4], [5, 5]   # Class 1
])
y_tree = np.array([0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1])

# Test different splits
feature = 0  # Feature 0
thresholds = [1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5]

print(f"\nDataset: {len(X_tree)} samples, 2 classes")
print(f"Parent entropy: {calculate_entropy(y_tree):.3f} bits")
print(f"\nTesting splits on Feature {feature}:")

best_threshold = None
best_ig = -1

for threshold in thresholds:
    ig = information_gain(X_tree, y_tree, feature, threshold)
    print(f"  Threshold = {threshold}: Information Gain = {ig:.4f} bits")
    if ig > best_ig:
        best_ig = ig
        best_threshold = threshold

print(f"\n✓ Best split: Feature {feature} <= {best_threshold} (IG = {best_ig:.4f})")

# Visualize the split
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))

# Plot 1: Data and best split
axes[0].scatter(X_tree[y_tree==0, 0], X_tree[y_tree==0, 1], 
                s=200, c='blue', marker='o', edgecolors='black', linewidth=2, label='Class 0')
axes[0].scatter(X_tree[y_tree==1, 0], X_tree[y_tree==1, 1], 
                s=200, c='red', marker='s', edgecolors='black', linewidth=2, label='Class 1')
axes[0].axvline(best_threshold, color='green', linestyle='--', linewidth=3, 
                label=f'Best split (x={best_threshold})')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Feature 0', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Feature 1', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_title(f'Decision Tree Split (IG={best_ig:.3f} bits)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 2: Information gain for each threshold
axes[1].plot(thresholds, [information_gain(X_tree, y_tree, feature, t) for t in thresholds], 
             'o-', linewidth=2.5, markersize=10, color='purple')
axes[1].axhline(0, color='gray', linestyle='--', linewidth=1)
axes[1].scatter([best_threshold], [best_ig], s=300, c='green', marker='*', 
                zorder=5, edgecolors='black', linewidth=2, label='Best split')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Threshold', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Information Gain (bits)', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_title('Finding Best Split', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('example1_decision_tree.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
print("\n✓ Saved Example 1 visualization")

"""
================================================================================
COMPLETE EXAMPLE 2: Feature Selection using Mutual Information
================================================================================
"""

print("\n" + "="*80)
print("COMPLETE EXAMPLE 2: Feature Selection with MI")
print("="*80)

from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
from sklearn.feature_selection import SelectKBest, mutual_info_classif

# Generate dataset with redundant features
X_feat, y_feat = make_classification(n_samples=500, n_features=20, 
                                      n_informative=5, n_redundant=10, 
                                      n_repeated=0, n_clusters_per_class=2,
                                      random_state=42)

# Calculate MI for all features
mi_all = mutual_info_classif(X_feat, y_feat, random_state=42)

# Select top 5 features
selector = SelectKBest(mutual_info_classif, k=5)
X_selected = selector.fit_transform(X_feat, y_feat)
selected_features = selector.get_support(indices=True)

print(f"\nGenerated dataset: {X_feat.shape[0]} samples, {X_feat.shape[1]} features")
print(f"  5 informative, 10 redundant, 5 useless")
print(f"\nTop 5 features by MI:")
top_indices = np.argsort(mi_all)[::-1][:5]
for i, idx in enumerate(top_indices, 1):
    print(f"  {i}. Feature {idx}: MI = {mi_all[idx]:.4f}")

# Visualize
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))

# Plot 1: MI scores for all features
feature_nums = np.arange(X_feat.shape[1])
colors_feat = ['green' if i in selected_features else 'lightgray' for i in range(len(mi_all))]

axes[0].bar(feature_nums, mi_all, color=colors_feat, alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Feature Index', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Mutual Information', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_title('Feature Selection: MI Scores', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')
axes[0].axhline(np.median(mi_all), color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                label='Median', alpha=0.7)
axes[0].legend(fontsize=11)

# Plot 2: Performance comparison
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score

# Train with all features
rf_all = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=50, random_state=42)
scores_all = cross_val_score(rf_all, X_feat, y_feat, cv=5)

# Train with selected features
rf_selected = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=50, random_state=42)
scores_selected = cross_val_score(rf_selected, X_selected, y_feat, cv=5)

methods_perf = ['All Features\n(20)', 'Top 5 by MI']
accuracies = [np.mean(scores_all), np.mean(scores_selected)]
errors = [np.std(scores_all), np.std(scores_selected)]

bars = axes[1].bar(methods_perf, accuracies, yerr=errors, capsize=10,
                    color=['lightcoral', 'lightgreen'], alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black', linewidth=2)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Cross-Validation Accuracy', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_title('Model Performance', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1].set_ylim(0.7, 1.0)
axes[1].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

for bar, acc in zip(bars, accuracies):
    height = bar.get_height()
    axes[1].text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, height + 0.02, 
                 f'{acc:.3f}', ha='center', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('example2_feature_selection.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
print(f"\n✓ Accuracy with all features: {np.mean(scores_all):.3f}")
print(f"✓ Accuracy with top 5 MI features: {np.mean(scores_selected):.3f}")
print("✓ Fewer features, similar performance!")
print("\n✓ Saved Example 2 visualization")

"""
================================================================================
COMPLETE EXAMPLE 3: Cross-Entropy Loss in Neural Network
================================================================================
"""

print("\n" + "="*80)
print("COMPLETE EXAMPLE 3: Cross-Entropy Loss in Action")
print("="*80)

# Simulate neural network training
np.random.seed(42)
n_epochs = 50
n_classes = 3

# True labels (one-hot)
true_labels = np.array([[1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1], [1, 0, 0]])  # 4 samples

# Simulate predictions improving over time
def softmax(x):
    exp_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=1, keepdims=True))
    return exp_x / np.sum(exp_x, axis=1, keepdims=True)

def cross_entropy_loss(y_true, y_pred):
    return -np.mean(np.sum(y_true * np.log(y_pred + 1e-10), axis=1))

# Initial random predictions
initial_logits = np.random.randn(4, 3)
initial_probs = softmax(initial_logits)

print(f"\nTraining {len(true_labels)} samples, {n_classes} classes")
print(f"Initial predictions:")
for i, (true, pred) in enumerate(zip(true_labels, initial_probs)):
    print(f"  Sample {i}: True={np.argmax(true)}, Pred={pred}, CE={cross_entropy_loss(true.reshape(1, -1), pred.reshape(1, -1)):.3f}")

# Simulate training
losses = []
for epoch in range(n_epochs):
    # Gradually improve predictions
    logits = initial_logits + epoch * 0.5 * (true_labels - 0.33)
    probs = softmax(logits)
    loss = cross_entropy_loss(true_labels, probs)
    losses.append(loss)

final_probs = softmax(initial_logits + (n_epochs-1) * 0.5 * (true_labels - 0.33))

print(f"\nFinal predictions:")
for i, (true, pred) in enumerate(zip(true_labels, final_probs)):
    print(f"  Sample {i}: True={np.argmax(true)}, Pred={pred}, CE={cross_entropy_loss(true.reshape(1, -1), pred.reshape(1, -1)):.3f}")

print(f"\n✓ Loss decreased: {losses[0]:.3f} → {losses[-1]:.3f}")

# Visualize
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))

# Plot 1: Training curve
axes[0].plot(losses, linewidth=3, color='blue')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Epoch', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Cross-Entropy Loss', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_title('Training Progress', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
axes[0].fill_between(range(len(losses)), losses, alpha=0.3, color='blue')

# Plot 2: Predictions before and after
samples_idx = np.arange(len(true_labels))
width_pred = 0.25

axes[1].bar(samples_idx - width_pred, np.argmax(true_labels, axis=1), width_pred, 
            label='True Label', color='green', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')
axes[1].bar(samples_idx, np.argmax(initial_probs, axis=1), width_pred, 
            label='Initial Pred', color='red', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')
axes[1].bar(samples_idx + width_pred, np.argmax(final_probs, axis=1), width_pred, 
            label='Final Pred', color='blue', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')

axes[1].set_xlabel('Sample Index', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Predicted Class', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_title('Predictions Improve with Training', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1].set_xticks(samples_idx)
axes[1].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[1].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('example3_neural_network.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
print("\n✓ Saved Example 3 visualization")

print("\n" + "="*80)
print("EXERCISES - INFORMATION THEORY")
print("="*80)

================================================================================
SOLUTIONS HINT:
================================================================================

Exercise 1:
a) H = log₂(4) = 2 bits (maximum entropy - uniform)

Exercise 2:

Exercise 3:

Exercise 4:

Exercise 5:

If IG > 0, split is useful!

================================================================================
KEY TAKEAWAYS - INFORMATION THEORY COMPLETE
================================================================================

🎯 CORE CONCEPTS:
-----------------

1. ENTROPY H(X)
   • Measures uncertainty/surprise
   • 0 = deterministic, max = uniform
   • Used in: Decision trees, compression

2. CROSS-ENTROPY H(P,Q)
   • Loss function for classification!
   • Measures cost of wrong distribution
   • Minimizing CE = Maximizing likelihood

3. KL DIVERGENCE KL(P||Q)
   • "Distance" between distributions
   • H(P,Q) = H(P) + KL(P||Q)
   • Used in: VAE, model comparison, RL

4. MUTUAL INFORMATION I(X;Y)
   • Measures dependence
   • Symmetric: I(X;Y) = I(Y;X)
   • Used in: Feature selection

🔥 ML APPLICATIONS:
-------------------

✓ Decision Trees → Information Gain (Entropy)
✓ Neural Networks → Cross-Entropy Loss
✓ VAE Regularization → KL Divergence
✓ Feature Selection → Mutual Information
✓ Language Models → Perplexity (exp(H))
✓ Compression → Entropy (optimal code length)

💡 RELATIONSHIPS:
-----------------
```
